newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU commission says veal premium must stay.
newsitem.headline: EU commission says veal premium must stay.

text.p: A veal early marketing premium must stay for now despite French claims that it is unfair, the European Commission said on Friday.
France had asked that the early marketing premium aimed at the slaughter of young veal calves should end because Paris says it favours Dutch producers whose animals are above average weight.

"Angry French farmers blocked a Dutch veal lorry before today's meeting of the beef management committee in protest but the Commission view is that it is too early to end the premium," an official said.
"Discussion on the question of the premium will continue and it is due to be reviewed in April," the official added.
The early marketing premium designed to encourage beef producers to take young animals out of production has been paid on 170,000 head mainly in the Netherlands, France and Germany.
A second calf processing premium also designed to ease market pressure following the mad cow crisis has been paid on 570 animals mainly in the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland.
